title: Counter-attack: choose the moment, avoid the half-way move
outcomes: Chooses between counter-attacking and defending by checking whether a supporting piece makes the counter faster
Sees that moving the supporting piece turns the same counter from winning to losing
Names the half-hearted third option and rejects it

steps.text: In **Counter-attack or defend: count both races** you counted the two races. Now choose the moment. A counter-attack comes when your defence is complete and your threat is faster. Do not drift into the **half-hearted third option**: a move that neither defends properly nor threatens something bigger. At each move say one word aloud before you play: counter or defend.

steps.caption: White threatens Rxf8 mate. Black has a counter with check.

line.say: Bxf1 takes the queen. Black has won a piece.

claims.statement: Rxf1+ is the engine's best move (depth 16).
Along the engine's best line Black comes out at least a piece ahead (depth 16).

steps.text: **A counter-attack holds** when your move comes with check or a threat he must answer, and a piece of yours supports the follow-up. It **fails** when it is one move slower or loses the supporting piece. The engine's moves in the contrast show this, not a general law: 'the best defence is attack' is a **rule of thumb**, and you have to count before you rely on it.

steps.title: One position, three small changes
steps.prompt: Black considers Qf2+. Predict for each: counter-attack or defend? Then check.
In your next game, when you are under pressure, write counter or defend before each move. Afterwards, find one move that was neither.
